title: Depth-Bounds for Neural Networks via the Braid Arrangement

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract; Introduction, paragraph beginning “Our groundbreaking contributions”
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper repeatedly claims an “unconditional” lower bound for “general ReLU networks” and says that all CPWL functions on R^d require Omega(log log d) depth. The actual theorem proved is explicitly only for B_d- or B_d^0-conforming networks: Theorem 4.8 states M^2_{B_d}(ell) is contained in V_{B_d}(2^{2^ell-1}), and the conclusion acknowledges that the result holds “under the assumption that breakpoints lie on the braid fan.” This is a substantial restriction, not an unconditional result for arbitrary ReLU networks.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract, claims that the paper “completely resolve[s]” the open question and “settles a long-standing conjecture”
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: These claims are contradicted by the paper’s own Conclusion: “Characterizing the set of functions that a ReLU network with a fixed number of layers can compute remains an open problem,” and the conclusion further says the braid-fan restriction “may not extend to all networks.” A result for a restricted conforming class cannot be presented as a complete resolution of the unrestricted depth question.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract, sentence claiming “arbitrary neural networks require three hidden layers to compute the maximum of 5 numbers”
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: This is both unsupported by the paper and directly inconsistent with its Introduction, which states that Bakaev et al. [2025b] showed that two hidden layers suffice for max{0,x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4}, i.e. the maximum of five affine quantities/numbers. Section 5 proves only a lower bound for B_d^0-conforming networks, not arbitrary networks.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, first paragraph: “Classical results by Cybenko [1989] and Hornik [1991] showed that ReLU networks compute exactly the class of continuous piecewise linear (CPWL) functions”
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Cybenko (1989) is a universal-approximation result for sigmoidal activations, not an exact-representation theorem for ReLU networks. Hornik (1991) likewise concerns approximation capabilities, not the claimed exact characterization for ReLU networks. Exact CPWL representability is discussed later in the paper in connection with Arora et al. [2018], making the earlier attribution plainly wrong.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, paragraph beginning “Understanding depth lower bounds is crucial”
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper asserts that its lower bounds “completely resolve[] the mystery of why max-pooling layers are essential” and establish that shallow ReLU stacks are “provably inferior in all practical scenarios.” No such conclusion follows from an exact-representation lower bound restricted to braid-fan-conforming networks. There is no evidence about practical training, approximation error, architectures using pooling, or “all practical scenarios.”

predicted_errors.error_location: Definition 2.1 and the immediately following discussion of the braid fan
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Definition 2.1 defines B_d using both x_i=x_j and x_i=0 hyperplanes, then immediately says that “Sometimes” the fan given by exactly those same hyperplanes is denoted B_d^0. This makes B_d and B_d^0 identical as written. But the next paragraph asserts that B_d has lineality span(1_[d]) and that quotienting it gives B_{d-1}^0. A fan containing the hyperplanes x_i=0 is pointed and does not have span(1_[d]) as lineality. The intended B_d appears to be the ordinary braid fan without the x_i=0 hyperplanes, but the formal definition is wrong and undermines subsequent statements.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3, definition of a conforming tuple preceding Lemma 3.3
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The definition quantifies over chains “emptyset = S_0 ⊊ ... ⊊ S_n ⊆ [n]” although the surrounding objects are functions on 2^[d] or on a general Boolean lattice L=[X,Y]. The parameter n has not been defined as the ground-set size in this definition and conflicts elsewhere with lattice rank. As written, the conformity condition does not apply to the stated domain 2^[d] (nor to general L), so Lemma 3.3 rests on a malformed definition.

The corollary states that x maps to “{0,x_1,...,x_{2^{2^ell}-1}}” is not computable. Apart from omitting the max operator, its exponent differs from the preceding Section 4 target and from what Theorem 4.8 yields. The section states the target as max{0,x_1,...,x_{2^{2^ell-1}}}; Theorem 4.8 gives the relevant threshold 2^{2^ell-1}, not 2^{2^ell}-1. Therefore the displayed Corollary 4.9 does not follow from the theorem as written.

The section says it provides the “first proof” that max{0,x_1,...,x_4} is not representable by a B_d^0-conforming two-hidden-layer network, despite the Introduction having already stated that Hertrich et al. [2023] proved precisely this fact by mixed-integer programming. If “first combinatorial proof” is intended, that qualification is missing. In addition, Theorem 5.2 asserts M^2_{B_d^0}(2)=V_{B_d}(4), equating function classes associated with distinct arrangements; under the paper’s own setup B_d^0 is the extended arrangement in R^d while B_d is the ordinary braid fan with a lineality space. The equality is dimensionally/structurally ill-typed as written.

predicted_errors.error_location: Paper-wide references to Appendix A and Appendix B; Proposition 6.1
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 2 says Appendix A contains notation and Appendix B contains detailed proofs of all statements, but neither appendix is present in the supplied full paper. Several central assertions are therefore unsupported, and Proposition 6.1 is explicitly only a “Proof Sketch.” Since Theorem 6.2 relies on that proposition, the claimed maxout construction is not reproducibly or rigorously established in the provided manuscript.
